body.statement: For every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\) and every \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\), the interval \(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\), which is a measurable function solely of \(D\) and known design quantities, obeys \(P_{Z,m}\{\theta\in I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\operatorname{len}\{I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\}\le2\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+(M/3)\log(2/\alpha)\}\).
body.justification: This is a genuinely reportable finite-sample interval: no latent block mean appears in the statistic or its endpoints.
body.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, gives Hoeffding intervals for four binary two-stage partial-interference effects, and RigdonHudgens2015 inverts randomization tests for those effects under stratified interference. Their designs and estimands differ from the observed-data All Treat versus All Control interval under fixed independent assignment on unequal cliques.
body.consumer: An analyst using full-neighborhood exposures obtains a computable finite-sample interval and sees when a single rare block controls length.
body.proof_tex:
Measurability follows from \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}block\text{-}means}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}ht}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}clipped\text{-}ht}\).  Summing the expectation identity in \(\mathrm{lem{:}block\text{-}reduction}\) and using the definition of \(\theta\) gives \(\mathbb E_Z\widehat\theta=\theta\).

We use a slightly sharper support calculation than the diameter bound stated in that lemma.  Put \(c_l=w_l/q_l\), \(u_l=c_l\mu_l(a)\), and \(v_l=-c_l\mu_l(b)\).  Then \(|u_l|,|v_l|\le c_l/2\) and \(X_l\) has values \(u_l,v_l,0\) with probabilities \(q_l,q_l,1-2q_l\).  For a realized value \(u_l\),
\[
 |u_l-\mathbb EX_l|=|(1-q_l)u_l-q_lv_l|
 \le(1-q_l){c_l\over2}+q_l{c_l\over2}={c_l\over2};
\]
the same holds for \(v_l\), while \(|0-\mathbb EX_l|=q_l|u_l+v_l|\le q_lc_l\le c_l/2\).  Thus \(|X_l-\mathbb EX_l|\le M/2\), and \(v:=\sum_l\operatorname{Var}(X_l)\le S/2\) by \(\mathrm{lem{:}block\text{-}reduction}\).

For a centered variable \(W\) with \(|W|\le b\), expansion of the exponential and \(|W|^k\le b^{k-2}W^2\) for \(k\ge2\) give
\[
 \log\mathbb E e^{zW}\le {z^2\mathbb EW^2\over2(1-bz/3)},\qquad 0\le z<3/b.
\]
Multiplying these moment-generating-function bounds for the independent centered summands, and using exponential Markov with \(b=M/2\), gives
\[
 P_Z\{\widehat\theta-\theta\ge y\}
 \le\exp\{-y^2/(2v+2by/3)\},
\]
and the same inequality holds for the lower tail.  The elementary Bernstein inversion, obtained by substituting \(y=\sqrt{2vx}+2bx/3\) in the preceding exponent, yields
\[
 P_Z\left\{|\widehat\theta-\theta|>
 \sqrt{2v\log(2/\alpha)}+{2b\over3}\log(2/\alpha)\right\}\le\alpha.
\]
Using \(2v\le S\) and \(2b\le M\) makes the displayed radius no larger than \(h_\alpha\).  Since \(\theta\in[-1,1]\) by the outcome support and \(\sum_lw_l=1\), clipping the interval to \([-1,1]\) cannot remove \(\theta\) on the concentration event.  Finally, the intersection of two intervals has length at most the smaller of their lengths, so
\[
 \operatorname{len}(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha})
 \le\min\{2,2h_\alpha\}=2\min\{1,h_\alpha\}.
\]
As an exact small-instance check, take \(n=3\), block sizes \((1,2)\), hence
\((w_1,w_2)=(1/3,2/3)\) and \((q_1,q_2)=(1/2,1/4)\).  Put
\((\mu_1(a),\mu_1(b))=(1/2,-1/2)\) and
\((\mu_2(a),\mu_2(b))=(-1/2,1/2)\).  Enumeration of all
\(2^3\) assignments gives \(X_1=1/3\) always, while \(X_2=-4/3\)
on either unanimous assignment of the second block and \(X_2=0\) on
either mixed assignment.  Thus
\[
 P_Z(\widehat\theta=-1)=P_Z(\widehat\theta=1/3)=1/2,\qquad
 \mathbb E_Z\widehat\theta=-1/3=\theta,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(\widehat\theta)=4/9\le S/2=1.
\]
This exhaustive check verifies mutual exclusion, both inverse-probability
factors, and clipping in the smallest unequal-block example.
